subject: Creativity
title: Creating Memorable Characters: The Want vs. Need Framework
description: One-minute skill: Creating Memorable Characters: The Want vs. Need Framework.

hook.text: A character wants a treasure. But what they need is self-worth. The gap between want and need drives every great story.

buildup.text: Want is external — the goal the character chases. Need is internal — the lesson they must learn but don't know they.

discovery.text: In Finding Nemo, Marlin wants to find his son. But he NEEDS to learn to let go.

twist.text: In tragedies, the character never recognizes their need. Macbeth wants power but needs to accept his own humanity.

climax.text: The moment a character's want and need collide — when pursuing the goal means facing the inner truth — is the story's.

punchline.text: Plot is what characters want. Story is what they need.

quiz.question: In the Want vs. Need framework, what drives the plot forward?

details.summary: The most compelling characters have a conscious want and an unconscious need that conflict. They pursue what they think they want while the story reveals what they actually need. This tension creates depth, internal conflict, and satisfying character arcs.
details.whyItMatters: The want versus need framework gives writers a reliable method for creating psychologically complex characters who feel real. It is the engine driving most great character arcs in literature and film.
takeaways: Want is what the character consciously pursues
Need is the deeper growth the character actually requires
The gap between want and need creates internal conflict

faq.question: Do the want and need always conflict?
faq.answer: In the most compelling stories, yes. When characters get what they want but not what they need, or vice versa, the tension creates drama. When want and need align from the start, there is less room for meaningful character growth.

faq.question: How do you discover a character's need?
faq.answer: Ask what character flaw is preventing them from being fulfilled. The need is usually the opposite of that flaw. A character who wants power might need humility. A character who wants isolation might need connection.
